label: early original-phase input of 0/m/z/b/u/w/q (first occurrence)
predicate: (phase == 0) & (t >= 1) & (t <= 5) & isin(in_tok, [tok("0"), tok("m"), tok("z"), tok("b"), tok("u"), tok("w"), tok("q")]) & (in_first == 1)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99.8% of mass), mostly at t=1..5 with a peak at t=3, never at t=0, and almost never at the delimiter or in the copy phase. It fires mainly on the first occurrence of an input token, with strong token preference: 0, m and z (5-6x lift), then b, u, w and q. It also depends on earlier context: it is boosted when the previous token is e, q, t or f, and when y, j, a or k appeared earlier (first_tok y gives 4.8x). The top activations look like y/j/k ... e followed by 0/m/z/q. Because the context dependence is distributed, it is not captured by a simple conjunction: adding the prev-token or seen-token conditions raises precision to about 0.14-0.23 but loses recall. The recorded predicate covers about 72% of activation mass on dev, but precision is only about 9% (F1 0.16): most early 0/m/z inputs do not activate it. Magnitude grows with the token/context match; this was not checked beyond the top examples.
